assumptions: Anchor is 'center' because boxes are top-down vehicles whose centre is metric position; bottom_center is only the downstream AABB edge, not wheels.
'shall stop' is encoded as DWELL with max_speed 0.05, i.e. continuously inside while fully stopped.
Minimum stopped time 1000 ms is assumed because the statute states no duration.
stop_zone, the last 10 metres before the line, is used as proxy for 'at the near side of the intersection at a clearly marked stop line'.
Only inbound crossings trigger the rule; per line geometry approaching from y<0.6 to y>0.6 (+y) is encoded as to_right.
No maximum gap between stop and crossing is enforced.
Objects that never cross the stop line vacuously pass, per 'must do A before B' idiom.
Exception 'Unless otherwise directed by a police officer or traffic control signal' cannot be seen by the camera and is omitted.
raw_output.normalized_explanation: Every vehicle that crosses the stop line inbound must first come to a complete stop inside the approach waiting zone.

provenance.reason: Boxes represent vehicles viewed from above; their centre is metric position, bottom_center is downstream AABB edge, not wheels, so centre is the point zones and lines were drawn for.

provenance.quote: at the near side of the intersection at a clearly marked stop line

provenance.reason: Statute says 'shall stop' with no duration; 1000 ms chosen as minimum continuous stopped time to detect a stop.

provenance.quote: at a clearly marked stop line

provenance.reason: Statute says 'approaching' but no detector direction; line info says approach from y<0.6 to y>0.6 (+y) is encoded as to_right, so inbound crossing is to_right.
Statute states no maximum time between stop and crossing; no limit enforced.

text: Unless otherwise directed by a police officer or traffic control signal, the driver of a vehicle approaching a stop sign at an intersection shall stop at the near side of the intersection at a clearly marked stop line.
